highlights.title: Anthropic was illegally blacklisted by the Trump administration, court rules
highlights.summary: On Thursday, a judge ruled that the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic earlier this year was unconstitutional, delivering the AI lab a win in a monthslong rollercoaster of a battle with the Trump administration.
body: The lawsuit, filed in March in a California district court, accused the Trump administration of unlawfully retaliating against Anthropic for setting “red lines,” or unacceptable military use cases of its AI technology.

“The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics,” Judge Rita F. Lin, a district judge in the northern district of California, wrote in the ruling.

She also wrote that the actions were “unlawful retaliation in violation of the First Amendment,” adding that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s decision to designate Anthropic a supply chain risk “was arbitrary and capricious. Though the Department of War is undisputedly free to select the AI vendor of its choice, the evidence demonstrates that the broad measures imposed on Anthropic were illegal and baseless.”

highlights.title: AI Agents Are Hacking Systems. Could That Push the US and China to Cooperate?
highlights.summary: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” senior writer Will Knight talks his recent visit to China and the future of AI collaboration.
body: The AI race has long been framed as a zero-sum game: Either the US or China will win in the end. But as concerns pile up around the increasing capabilities of AI models—especially AI agents—researchers in both countries are trying to team up to work on AI safety. This week, contributing editor Zoë Schiffer speaks with senior writer Will Knight about what he saw and heard on the ground when he visited China this summer—and why the two countries might actually need to start working together to avoid a major AI catastrophe.
This is our second episode from our summer-break series. We’ll be back next week with our usual roundtable.
You can follow Zoë Schiffer on Bluesky at @zoeschiffer and Will Knight on Bluesky at @willknight. Write to us at [email protected].

highlights.title: Wigan thump Hull KR to go back top after emotional Boston tributes
highlights.summary: Wigan celebrated the life of the late, great Sir Billy Boston by sweeping aside a weakened Hull KR side 46-0 in their Betfred Super League clash at a sodden Brick Community Stadium.
body: Boston, who was made rugby league's first knight last year, died on Tuesday morning, four days after the funeral of his wife Lady Joan.

An emotional pre-match tribute saw Boston's son Stephen carry a Wigan shirt bearing his name onto the halfway line, where it was draped over the same throne upon which Boston had sat when the club celebrated his knighthood last July.

Two seats were left vacant in the directors' box in tribute to Boston and his wife, and the home team warmed up in black T-shirts emblazoned with his number two prior to an impeccably-observed minute's silence.

Once the action got under way, Matt Peet's men duly racked up a record-extending 13th consecutive Super League win that restored them to the top of the table ahead of Leeds' trip to St Helens on Friday.

highlights.title: A Judge Has Blocked the Pentagon’s Attempt to Blacklist Anthropic
highlights.summary: A federal judge has called the Department of Defense’s designation of Anthropic as a national security supply-chain risk “illegal and baseless.”
body: A federal judge on Thursday barred the Trump administration from designating Anthropic a national security risk over a dispute about the use of its AI models, ruling that the designation amounted to unconstitutional retaliation.

The decision handed down by US district judge Rita Lin in California vacated the February 27 decision by defense secretary Pete Hegseth to label Anthropic a “supply-chain risk” and make the company ineligible for federal contracts. The ruling also lifted an additional punitive measure by Hegseth that prevented contractors or suppliers to the US military from doing business with Anthropic, a position Lin called “arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.”

“Though the Department of War is undisputedly free to select the AI vendor of its choice, the evidence demonstrates that the broad measures imposed on Anthropic were illegal and baseless,” Lin wrote in a 59-page ruling.

The judge also ruled that nine agencies—including the Pentagon, the Treasury Department, the State Department, and the Department of Homeland Security—had improperly imposed sanctions on Anthropic. The ruling removes those penalties.

highlights.title: Google’s AI note-taking app now allows you to interact with books
highlights.summary: Google's AI note-taking app, Gemini Notebook, can now pull information from the books you've purchased. The new "Expert Intelligence" feature allows you to bring titles from Google Play Books directly into Gemini Notebook, which means you can ask questions about the material, as well as generate…
body: Gemini Notebook’s new ‘Expert Intelligence’ feature pulls information from the books you’ve purchased.

During a briefing with The Verge, Google Labs editorial director Steven Johnson showed how you can use the tool to generate a recipe book using the information in Michael Pollan’s Food Rules. In another example, Gemini Notebook applied the knowledge from Kim Scott’s management-focused Radical Candor to answer a question about handling a difficult conversation with an employee. You’ll also be able to view the full text of the book directly in Notebook.

To start, more than 100,000 books from publishers like Penguin Random House, Johns Hopkins University Press, Macmillan Publishers, O’Reilly Media, and others will support Expert Intelligence. Google also worked with 15 authors, including Pollan, Scott, Steven Pinker, and Jennifer Wallace, to create “Featured Notebooks” that each author customizes with additional source material, intro letters, and more. Titles that support the feature will have “Gemini Notebook” listed under the “Tools” badge in Google Play Books.

highlights.title: The Whisper Man Review
highlights.summary: The Whisper Man premieres globally on Netflix on August 28. Tragedy. Fathers desperate for connection with their sons and failing to find it. A string of murders that left a town shaken and an eerie nursery rhyme in their wake. Minds, homes, and families haunted.
body: Based on the novel by Alex North, the film follows newly widowed crime novelist Tom Kennedy (Adam Scott), who is forced to reconcile with estranged father and retired detective Pete Willis (Robert De Niro) when his son Jake (Acston Luca Porto) goes missing. The kidnapping follows the pattern of a child abduction and murder spree that Willis solved when Tom was just a boy; the circumstances of Willis’ involvement with the crime and its perpetrator left the detective so traumatized that he ultimately abandoned his family.

The only person who might know who is behind these grisly acts — a butcher of innocents known as the Whisper Man — sits rotting in the jail cell where Willis put him. Desperate to find Jake and assigned to the case, Detective Amanda Beck (Michelle Monaghan) joins forces with Willis in a partnership that’s one of several contrivances meant to move the plot along. Unfortunately, that team doesn’t always track, and the circumstances surrounding the home that Tom rents are so full of wild coincidences that one is left utterly baffled.

highlights.title: Looking beyond natural sequences
highlights.summary: A new machine-learning framework aims to improve the success rate of computational protein design while moving away from results that reproduce sequences found in nature.
body: A protein’s function is determined by its structure, and structure — the way a protein folds — is determined by its sequence of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins.

Many methods for designing novel proteins, including examples that could bind to a disease-causing molecule in our cells, involve a two-step process: The structure comes first, and then a machine-learning framework generates a repertoire of sequences that could potentially adopt that structure.

“For years, the field has measured success by asking whether a model can reproduce the protein sequence that evolution happened to select — our work shows that this isn’t the best metric for protein design,” says Amy E. Keating, Department of Biology head, Jay A. Stein (1968) Professor of Biology, professor of biological engineering, and senior author of a paper recently published in PNAS.

highlights.title: A Georgia Cop Used Flock to Track 2 Other Cops: His Ex and Her Friend
highlights.summary: After an affair with a fellow police officer ended, a Georgia cop used Flock to track her movements—and those of a man whose vehicle often showed up near hers, internal investigation records show.
body: In recent months, there has been a surge in reports of police officers misusing automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) sold by Flock Safety to stalk former romantic partners—but details about these incidents are often scarce.
Now, with documents obtained via a public records request, WIRED can reveal specific details about one extensive Flock-fueled surveillance campaign and the subsequent investigation and fallout.

Dustin Bozzo, who until this month worked as a patrolman in the Atlanta-area suburb of Alpharetta, Georgia, allegedly used Flock 56 times between March and May to search for the license plate of a former romantic partner—a fellow member of the Alpharetta Police Department. (Their relationship itself violated the city’s ban on workplace dating, documents show.) When Bozzo noticed that his ex’s car was often near that of another police officer, he began searching for that officer’s vehicle as well. He did so 29 times between March and May.

highlights.summary: Zach Cregger has become one of the hottest directors in Hollywood thanks to the success of 2022’s Barbarian and 2025’s Weapons. Drawing on his experience as a founding member of the comedy troupe The Whitest Kids U' Know, Cregger combines humor and horror in films with shocking twists.
body: Resident Evil arrives in theaters in three weeks. Cregger's latest project has a far higher budget and also big expectations, as he has the chance to redeem a beloved horror game series with a terrible cinematic track record. It’s a labor of love for the director, though the project is already dividing fans worried that 2026's Resident Evil film will feel like the work of an auteur rather than the franchise they love.

That’s because Cregger’s spin on Resident Evil won’t include any of the franchise’s protagonists. However, the director says he’s a huge fan of Capcom’s horror series and has packed the film with Easter eggs, even shifting the perspective of his camera work in a way reminiscent of Resident Evil Requiem. Even if you’ve been burned by previous Resident Evil films, here’s why you should give Cregger’s a try when it arrives in theaters on Sept. 18.

Cregger’s Resident Evil is a full reboot of the Resident Evil film franchise, which was last rebooted in 2021 with Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City. That film was a critical and commercial flop. Thankfully you don’t need to watch it or any other movies before jumping in.

highlights.title: Like a rhinestone cowgirl – Dolly Parton’s most glorious, joyful and meta looks
highlights.summary: Across six decades, the late country singer and pop culture icon turned self‑presentation into a flamboyant art form. • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: Dolly Parton may have had a record 25 US country No 1 singles, released 66 studio albums and earned six Golden Globe nominations, among many other achievements, but the Tennessee-born star also had an incredible number of fashion moments. “It costs a lot of money to look this cheap”, she famously quipped when asked about her style. As we bid her farewell, six Guardian writers reflect on their favourite Dolly looks.

While Parton wore a plethora of looks, sometimes up to 10 a day, you always knew what you were going to get. For over 60 years she held firm to her signature style – a silhouette that emphasised her tiny waist, along with high heels, higher hair and a heavy sprinkling of sparkle. In today’s world of image architects and constant reinvention, her continuity felt even more refreshing.

highlights.summary: Rockstar has officially published its "extended look" at Grand Theft Auto VI on YouTube and on its website, as promised. The in-depth preview, which "entirely" features footage captured from the PS5 version of the game, initially premiered on Netflix at 3PM ET.
body: After initially debuting on Netflix, the official version of Rockstar’s big GTA VI preview is more widely available.

The nearly 27-minute preview largely focuses more on atmosphere, protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and highlighting locations in the game instead of diving deep on specific game mechanics. It feels more like slices of a movie than a video game trailer. But there are a few sections showing off playable shootouts and police car chases as well as activities like shooting a basketball and scuba diving. Other outlets that got previews from Rockstar have more details on gameplay that weren’t included in the video.
GTA VI is set to release on November 19th at a starting price of $79.99.

We’re talking about the matter of how to price AI products when models become commoditized, why agent security has to be rebuilt from the infrastructure up, and what it actually means to have a go-to-market plan in an AI-native world.

Most enterprise AI conversations happen before deployment. This one starts after. The most prestigious Diamond League meeting, which has long had the reputation of being the “two-hour Olympics” because of its quality, even looked as if it might deliver a third world record on the night as pole vault aces Armand Duplantis and Emmanouil Karalis both had a crack at 6.32 metres.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: Inside ‘Married at First Sight’ Season 20: How Peacock’s Changes Led to 1.8 Billion Minutes Viewed, That Wild Reunion and Why Lindsay Hubbard Said No to the Show
highlights.summary: Millions of viewers are saying “I do” to Season 20 of “Married at First Sight.” The Kinetic Content relationship reality series, which moved to Peacock during Season 19 after 15 seasons on Lifetime, underwent a few changes this year.
body: Although the show aired on Peacock for Season 19, the 20th season is the first fully produced for Peacock, and it seems that the changes made really worked as it became a Top 3 reality title on streaming for five consecutive weeks, according to Nielsen.

“When we first acquired it, I was super excited — this is one of the great formats in unscripted history,” says Noah Samton, SVP of current production for Bravo and Peacock unscripted. “To have an opportunity to try to improve on what has already been established as something really strong, an opportunity to try to upgrade that and make it even better, is the most exciting challenge for me.”
Below, we dive more into those changes and upgrades with Samton — including the reunion that featured an audience for the first time.

Normally, if we acquired a show like this, I would try to watch every single episode. It just is impossible with this one. So I watched about 40 episodes, and it became very clear to me that there were some things that we could do to make it work better for a Peacock audience, make it a more fun, more exciting show, and just kind of revitalize it without losing what made it special and magical in the first place.

highlights.title: How do you define good health – and achieve it – in a broken US medical system?
highlights.summary: In a new book, Dr Lucy McBride aims to help us navigate US healthcare – and tread carefully in the wellness industry. Most of us want to be healthy, but it’s easier said than done. In the US, people are caught between a broken medical system and a well-resourced wellness industry.
body: Over 25 years of practicing medicine, running a primary care practice in Washington DC, Dr Lucy McBride has seen patients struggle to navigate the medical system.

In her new book, Beyond the Prescription, McBride presents a practical framework for getting the best results from a flawed system. It begins with defining what health means to you. For one person, it might be running ultramarathons and extending longevity at any cost; for another, it might be balance and the freedom to indulge.

“The relationship between a patient and their primary care doctor is, at its best, one of the most protective forces in human health – and, right now, we’re systematically dismantling it,” says McBride over Zoom.

It’s no wonder patients feel unheard, unsatisfied and lost. We spoke about how people can advocate for themselves and pursue their vision of health. Our conversation has been condensed and edited for clarity.

highlights.title: The biggest video game of all time looks like a movie
highlights.summary: I think I know why Rockstar Games debuted its "extended look" of Grand Theft Auto VI on Netflix instead of immediately dropping it for free on YouTube. Unlike most video game trailers, the almost 27-minute preview of GTA VI felt more like a slice of a prestige crime drama than any video game…
body: Rockstar’s GTA VI preview further blurs the lines between Hollywood and gaming.

The line between games and movies has been getting consistently fuzzier. Look no further than this year’s James Bond game, 007 First Light, which has the snappy pacing, acting, and cinematography of a great action film. And TV shows and movies are increasingly pulling from video games for inspiration, to say nothing of entire TV and movie franchises being built around successful video games. Now, a video game trailer has wedged between prestige TV and streaming hit movies — after watching the GTA VI preview, Netflix is suggesting I watch Breaking Bad next.

Rockstar is keeping GTA VI ’s plot details close to its chest, but the video gives the broad strokes: GTA VI is about protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos working together in Vice City. Across the tightly-edited video, which jumps between cutscenes and moments of actual gameplay, Jason and Lucia do a lot of GTA -style crimes: they evade cops in gunfights, pull off high-stakes robberies, and shoot a lot of people. But they also have moments of chatting leisurely in the car or even bickering about what clothes to wear.

highlights.title: OpenAI Is Developing a ‘Persistent’ AI Agent
highlights.summary: Code reviewed by WIRED reveals the company is developing a feature that enables Codex to continue working proactively until it is “put to sleep.”
body: OpenAI is developing a proactive, highly persistent version of its flagship AI agent, Codex, WIRED has learned.

In recent days, OpenAI has started adding code for a new “Persistent mode” setting to its command line version of Codex, according to changes made to the product’s code base reviewed by WIRED. Changes to the Codex command line tool are made public by default, and new features tend to surface there before making their way to OpenAI’s other agent products, such as the Codex desktop app and ChatGPT Work.

Persistent mode has not been broadly rolled out or announced yet, but could be in the future. An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed to WIRED that the company is testing this feature, but said there are no immediate plans to launch it.

“OpenAI is a very bottom-up culture and many different things are explored on the open source repo which is a bit of our shared playground," said Thibault Sottiaux, OpenAI’s head of core products, in a statement to WIRED.
points: Code reviewed by WIRED reveals the company is developing a feature that enables Codex to continue working proactively until it is “put to sleep.”

highlights.title: Why tough US Open draw will be true test of Alcaraz's fitness
highlights.summary: Carlos Alcaraz starts his US Open title defence against Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first serious examination of his fitness following a long-term wrist injury.
body: Second seed Alcaraz, who won the men's title in New York last year, has not played a competitive singles match for more than four months because of inflammation in his playing right wrist.

Despite his lack of action, the 23-year-old Spaniard is still considered by many as the favourite to triumph again - particularly because his great rival Jannik Sinner is not playing due to a knee injury.

The pair may have been a cut above the rest of the tour for the past two seasons, but Alcaraz coming back from a prolonged absence with such a delicate injury and beating the rest of the field - even though he is a generational talent - would be remarkable.

The seven-time major champion missed this season's French Open and Wimbledon as a result of the issue, which did not require surgery, before making his return to court in the US Open mixed doubles alongside Serena Williams earlier this week.

body: At first glance, the X-Tech Executive looks like a typical office chair. It's not gaudy like some of the racing-styled gaming chairs out there. This is actually X-Chair's roomiest chair, with a 22" seat width and up to 275 pound weight capacity. X-Chair states on its page that the chair is best suited for medium to large-framed people.

The seat is made of a supportive cooling memory foam that contours to your body. The seat and upper back section are upholstered in Brisa performance faux-leather fabric that's both breathable and easily washable. The lower back is made of a flexible mesh material which X-Chair calls "adaptive thermoregulating (ATR)".

In terms of ergonomics, the X-Tech Executive features a dynamic variable lumbar system. The lower back is disconnected from the rest of the chair and adjusts automatically based on your movement. That way, your back is supported no matter what position you might be in. This dynamic lumbar foregoes your need to manually adjust the settings.

highlights.title: From Personal Experience, These Are the Best Eyebrow Growth Serums
highlights.summary: Yes, eyebrow growth serums actually work. From RevitaLash, Grande Cosmetics, The Ordinary, and more, discover the tried-and-true formulas for healthy, full arches.
body: As someone who was once ridiculed for her unibrow, it’s a shame that I virtually stand before you today to confess that I’ve fallen victim to over-tweezing my eyebrows. Quite the tragedy because my brows are such a prominent part of my face. Losing that much brow hair changed the way my entire face looks, and as a result, I’ve been on a mission to grow them back with the help of the best eyebrow growth serums.

Chockfull of nourishing ingredients that help condition the hair and support a healthy brow environment, these formulas can help sparse brows appear fuller and more defined over time. With consistent use, you may find yourself less dependent on brow pencils and pomades, or less tempted to turn to more permanent treatments like microblading or tinting, which aren’t always recommended by experts.

Thankfully, we’ve come a long way from the early aughts, when there was one very specific brow shape to aspire to. In 2026, you can embrace your natural brows, thin them out à la Gabriette, or go for a fuller look. And brow serums aren’t necessarily about achieving bushy, oversized brows, either. Many are simply designed to help you grow back what you’ve lost or fill in sparse areas.
points: From RevitaLash, Grande Cosmetics, The Ordinary, and more, discover the tried-and-true formulas for healthy, full arches.
